memory_update.text: DSGX is the cleanest US-listed underfollowed software/data candidate for the tariff, sanctions, customs, and country-of-origin compliance stack because its products directly cover global trade intelligence, customs/regulatory compliance, tariff/duty data, and denied-party screening.

EXPD and CHRW are second-order logistics-compliance candidates: tariff volatility may not primarily lift freight demand, but can increase customs brokerage, trade consulting, analytics, classification, and restricted-party screening needs.

DNB is a speculative-shadow candidate: sanctions, beneficial-ownership, and supplier-risk data overlap with the compliance stack, but direct customs/tariff exposure must be verified before later-layer survival.

This node appears to split into three investable sub-lanes: direct GTM software/data, logistics customs brokerage/compliance services, and entity/supplier-risk data used for sanctions and restricted-party screening.

E2open/Amber Road would have been a strong US-listed GTM software candidate, but ETWO was acquired by WiseTech Global in August 2025 and is no longer independently US-listed; WiseTech remains a non-US reference anchor rather than a US-listed candidate.

Testing/inspection/certification firms such as SGS, Bureau Veritas, and Intertek have strong traceability and forced-labor compliance relevance but are not clean US-listed small/mid-cap candidates; they may be reference comparables or ADR/OTC watchlist items in a non-US pass.

node: Tariff, sanctions, customs, and country-of-origin compliance stack
summary: Layer 1B underfollowed expansion for the tariff/sanctions/customs compliance node. The most relevant US-listed discovery candidates are not manufacturers exposed to tariffs directly, but software/data and logistics-compliance intermediaries that monetize regulatory complexity: denied-party screening, HTS/classification, rules-of-origin, customs filing, supplier-risk monitoring, and brokerage/compliance workflow. Descartes Systems is the cleanest listed software/data match; Expeditors and C.H. Robinson are logistics/brokerage compliance beneficiaries; Dun & Bradstreet is a weaker but plausible third-party-risk/sanctions-data hypothesis. Thomson Reuters and WiseTech/e2open are important reference anchors, but Thomson Reuters is too large/broad and e2open is no longer independently US-listed after its 2025 acquisition by WiseTech.
